title: Requirement Fulfillment
measures: Whether the code the student wrote for each of their tasks meets the task's acceptance criteria.
inputs: the student's tasks with acceptance criteria (Scrum board)
the student's own cleaned changed lines (never a teammate's code)
computation: A LangGraph sub-agent judges every criterion with student-only tools (search their changes, read a hunk) and gives a verdict (met / partly / not met / cannot tell) citing the lines it saw; a critic of another model family challenges verdicts; plain code rejects a 'met' or 'partly' without valid cited lines. Criterion values met 1, partly 0.5, otherwise 0; task value = mean; sprint score = mean over the student's tasks. Tasks not started cost no model call and count 0.
output_scale: 0 = nothing of the criteria implemented, 1 = every criterion met.
gates: Provisional: only tasks that are Done or In Review are judged.
Not available without a language-model client or when no task has acceptance criteria.
validation: Development smoke on 10 tasks of a synthetic benchmark only: the critic version had task-level MAE 0.34. No held-out run was completed (language-model daily limits). The band reported is therefore rough, and the score should be read as an AI judgement to be sampled by a lecturer.
limits: Depends on a language model; verdicts can be wrong or inconsistent between runs.
Sees only the student's changes, not the code around them, so a criterion implemented in a teammate's file is not credited.
Acceptance criteria written vaguely produce vague verdicts.

warnings.could not be decided: Some criteria came back 'cannot tell': the agent was not shown enough code.
warnings.not judged: A task failed (model quota or error) and is not in the score.

typical_problems.symptom: task value 0 although the student says it is done
typical_problems.likely_cause: commits are not linked to the task, or the work is in a teammate's commits
large diffs or generated files hide the relevant code

typical_problems.symptom: score changes a lot between two runs on the same evidence
